components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; font: 500 14px/20px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.005em; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color .15s, color .15s; outline: none; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--ring, #d6246e); } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, #d6246e); color: var(--primary-foreground, #fff); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary, #d6246e) 90%, transparent); }

components.css: .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; column-gap: 10px; align-items: center; width: 460px; height: 68px; padding: 0 14px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--background, #fff); color: var(--foreground, #1d1b16); font: 400 14px/20px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; transition: background-color .15s; } .ds-row:hover { background: var(--row-hover, #f4f4f2); } .ds-row:active { background: var(--row-selected, #ebebe8); } .ds-bar { width: 2px; height: 12px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #3b82f6; align-self: start; margin-top: 4px; } .ds-row-main { min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-row-top { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: baseline; } .ds-row-top b { font-weight: 600; } .ds-addr { font-size: 12px; color: var(--subtle-foreground, #6b6a67); } .ds-row-top time { margin-left: auto; font: 400 12px/16px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-row-sub { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; min-width: 0; } .ds-txt { flex: 1; min-width: 0; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-txt i { font-style: normal; color: var(--muted-foreground, #5f5e5b); } .ds-chip { padding: 0 6px; border-radius: 4px; background: color-mix(in srgb, #3b82f6 16%, transparent); color: #1d4ed8; font-size: 12px; line-height: 18px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-count { font-size: 12px; color: var(--subtle-foreground, #6b6a67); }

narrative.overview:
Raven is a tidy, warm work surface for someone who lives in email all day. Everything is in reach and nothing shouts. The sidebar and canvas are a slightly darker warm stone. The list and reader sit on it as plain white paper, so the structure comes from tone, not boxes or shadows. Colour is rationed: one accent marks the primary action, the unread dot and links. Everything else is warm ink on warm neutrals.

Density is a feature, not a compromise. The reference pair is Notion Mail's calm and Outlook's density and clarity: many rows on screen, each readable at a glance, with selection shown by a flat tone shift rather than a highlight colour. The interface stays quiet so the mail can be loud.

There is one structure. The raven, classic and minimal presets change only the accent colour (magenta, copper, or ink), never layout, radius or material. Raven rejects skeuomorphism (bevels, 3D chrome, gradient title bars) and busy, colourful toolbar chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutrals with one rationed accent per preset.
Flat surfaces separated by tone and hairline borders; shadows only on floating layers.
System font, small sizes, and weight (not size) for hierarchy.
Gently rounded, consistent corners derived from one 8px base.
Full light and dark parity: every token has a night counterpart.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Each preset has exactly one accent. Use it only for the actions, selection and state listed above. Never use a second brand colour, and never use the accent as decoration or as a pane-sized fill.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Tint Rule
rules.body: Hover and selection are neutral tone shifts (Soft Stone, then Pressed Stone), never accent-tinted backgrounds.

rules.name: The Contrast Pair Rule
rules.body: Any accent used as text uses its -text variant. Every preset pair is checked for WCAG AA: the label on the accent fill is at least 4.5:1, and accent text on paper is at least 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside dense views comes from weight (400, 500 and 600) and colour (Warm Ink, Graphite, Pencil), not from bigger type. Unread rows get weight, not size. Keep bold (700) rare.

rules.name: The Two-Size Rule
rules.body: Inside the list, the reader chrome and menus, use only Body (14px) and Label (12px). Larger sizes belong to headlines.

rules.name: The Glass-Behind-Paper Rule
rules.body: On macOS, glass shows only where the canvas would be (sidebar, title bar, gutters). Reading and working surfaces (cards, dialogs, compose) stay opaque Paper, and floating layers get a frosted, mostly opaque tint, never clear glass.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Panes, rows, cards and buttons have no shadow. A shadow means "this floats above the page and will go away", which applies only to menus and dialogs.

rules.name: The One Base Rule
rules.body: Never hard-code a radius. Derive it from --radius, so a single value controls the whole form language.

dos: Do reference colour through tokens (bg-background, text-muted-foreground, var(--primary)), so every preset and dark mode stays correct.
Do give every new colour token a dark counterpart and an AA-checked contrast pair.
Do show hover and selection as neutral tone shifts (Soft Stone, then Pressed Stone).
Do keep panes flat and separate them with tone and 1px hairlines.
Do reach for Body (14px) and Label (12px) first, and use weight for emphasis.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion. Keep motion to short fades and 4–8px slides (0.2–0.4s, ease-out).
donts: Don't use skeuomorphism: bevels, 3D chrome, gradient title bars, or the old Express look.
Don't add busy chrome: colourful toolbars, rows of heavy filled icons, or promotional clutter.
Don't introduce a second accent colour or use the accent as a large background fill.
Don't add shadows to panes, rows, cards or buttons.
Don't add per-theme structural CSS. Presets change colour tokens only.
Don't hard-code hex values in components. The avatar tones are the single documented exception; account and label colours come from user data.
